messages:
Alex: Quick sync — view-router contract for dashboards + query layer. We keep hitting a perf vs correctness tradeoff around RBAC checks and caching. Wanted to lay out a proposal and get quick 👍/concerns before we lock for the sprint.

Alex: Problem summary: our current flow does query -> post-filter by permissions. That means cached view responses are tenant-dependent and cache hit rate collapses for multi-tenant dashboards. Observed: cache hit down from ~72% to ~41% on some heavy-report orgs after adding row-level post-filter. p50 increased ~18ms -> ~60ms on dashboard page loads (real numbers from last week's perf run).

Mira: Yeah we've seen the same. Post-filtering is simple and correct, but blows up billing & latency. Pre-filtering requires translating RBAC rules into query predicates which is tricky for complex polices.

Ryan: Two practical constraints: 1) some views are materialized system-level aggregations (=> can't pre-filter per tenant), 2) cross-tenant exports (admin) must remain correct even if slower.

Zara: Proposal idea: hybrid approach. Default pre-filter for tenant-scoped views (better cacheability), and fall back to post-filter for system/batch/admin endpoints. Also add a "permission-hash" cache key component so we don't leak data across tenants and still get decent hit rates for common roles.

Alex: Rough API/contract sketch:
```
GET /v1/views/:id?scope={tenant,system}
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
ViewRouter->resolve(viewId, user, scope) -> {query, cache_key_prefix, requires_post_filter: bool}
```
Where `cache_key_prefix` includes `tenant_id` and optionally `perm_hash` when using pre-filter.

Mira: For the `perm_hash` we should be explicit: hash of (role_ids + feature_flags + org_policy_version). That makes invalidation straightforward when permissions change.

Ryan: Tradeoffs: pre-filtering requires us to maintain a translator from policy to DB predicates. That's extra code and risk of divergence. Post-filter is slower but always correct. Hybrid means more surface area (we need both code paths).

Alex: Implementation plan (sprint-sized):
- Week 1: implement `perm_hash` and extend cache keys, add `requires_post_filter` flag to view manifest config.
- Week 2: implement pre-filter translator for the 80% simple policies (tenant read/write, role-based column filters). Keep complex rules routed to post-filter.
- Week 3: integration tests + perf harness + canary.

Zara: Canary strategy: feature flag `view-router-v2` + rollout to beta orgs first. DevOps: add a canary alert if cache hit drops >5% or p95 latency increases >20% for flagged orgs.

DevOps-bot: Canary alert rule created: `view_router_v2_canary` (oncall paging if p95 > 250ms OR cache_hit_drop > 0.05 for 15m).

Mira: RBAC ordering decision: For tenant-scoped dashboard routes we do pre-filter + quick sanity post-filter assert (sampled) in CI. For system/admin routes we keep post-filter only. This reduces risk while restoring cache hits.

Ryan: One more ops note: pre-filtered queries will push more selective predicates into DB, so we should test DB plan stability and index coverage. Add `EXPLAIN` collection to perf harness and look for plan regressions.

Alex: Backwards compatibility: we'll keep current behavior unless `view-router-v2` is enabled. Also add a migration lock for view manifests so authors can mark a view as `requires_post_filter: true` if they have complex policies.

Zara: Metrics to track during rollout: cache_hit_ratio (by org+flag), view_latency_p50/p95, db_cpu_seconds, number_of_post_filters_invoked, perm_hash_misses.

Mira: Follow-ups: I can draft the RFC addendum covering the translator shape + failure modes. Ryan / Alex: can you own the perf harness changes? Zara: you'll own the canary/alerting config.

Alex: Decision (consensus): implement hybrid pre-filter default for tenant-scoped views + post-filter for system/admin. Rollout behind `view-router-v2` feature flag with canary metrics. Action items assigned as above.

Alex: Final quick checklist for the sprint ticket:
- [ ] perm_hash + cache key change (Mira)
- [ ] pre-filter translator for simple policies (Ryan)
- [ ] fallback post-filter path + manifest flag (Ryan)
- [ ] perf harness & EXPLAIN capture (Alex/Ryan)
- [ ] canary alert rules (Zara)
- [ ] RFC addendum + docs (Mira)

Ryan: 👍 Good plan. I'll open PRs for translator + tests tomorrow.

Zara: 👍 I'll add the alert runbook as well.

Mira: 👍 will start RFC draft, include examples of policy -> predicate mappings.

Alex: Thanks all — I'll put the ticket in the sprint and link to this thread. :thumbsup:
